claims.text: Incorporating a small fraction of MoS2 nanoparticles into a high-entropy-alloy matrix will reduce both coefficient of friction and wear rate across a wide service-temperature range.
An MoS2 loading of 1–5 vol% is an appropriate intervention range.
Introducing MoS2 nanoparticles during alloy fabrication will produce a uniform dispersion within the high-entropy-alloy matrix.
MoS2 nanoparticles act as solid lubricants during sliding.
The dispersed MoS2 nanoparticles will form a low-shear-strength tribofilm at the contact interface.
The MoS2-derived tribofilm will reduce direct metal-to-metal contact.
Reduced direct metal-to-metal contact will lower both coefficient of friction and wear rate.
MoS2 has sufficient thermal stability to remain an effective lubricant over the proposed temperature range.
The MoS2-modified alloy will have at least 30% lower coefficient of friction than the untreated alloy under identical conditions.
The MoS2-modified alloy will have at least 30% lower wear rate than the untreated alloy under identical conditions.
The intervention will remain effective under dry sliding from room temperature through approximately 800°C.
Corrosive environments may prevent the proposed intervention from remaining effective.
Extreme loads may degrade the MoS2 nanoparticles and prevent the intervention from remaining effective.
Uniform dispersion of MoS2 nanoparticles may be difficult to achieve and may affect the tribological outcome.
The stability of MoS2 during prolonged high-temperature operation is uncertain and may affect the tribological outcome.
